title: Staged switchover validation playbooks and Terraform DR test module
author: Priya Nair
release_notes:
- Added staged switchover validation playbooks for on-prem/VPC deployments.
- New Terraform module to run dry-run and failover validation in CI.
- Helm hooks and chart tweaks to surface health endpoints during switchover tests.
- Docs: runbook and quick reference for run-and-rollback procedures.
description:
Motivation: Runbooks-as-code and automated, staged switchover tests are required to bring Private installs to a repeatable DR posture. This PR introduces a lightweight, opinionated set of validation playbooks and a Terraform testing module that together let SREs and operators rehearse multi-AZ switchover and automated partial failovers without affecting production data paths.

What this changes: added an ansible-based staged switchover playbook (installer/ansible/playbooks/dr-validation.yml) that performs progressively broader steps: control-plane failover, scheduling node evacuation, service routing validation, and optional data-restore dry-runs. A complementary Terraform test module (installer/terraform/modules/dr-test) can be invoked by CI or by customers to spin up ephemeral validation infra (VPC peering, test namespaces, test load generators) and run the playbooks against it.

Helm changes: several small chart updates to support switchover tests without full-scale deploys. We add a switchover readiness probe endpoint and a post-install hook that wires a temporary test-config map used exclusively for validation runs (charts/redwood-private/templates/switchover-hook.yaml and values.yaml toggles). These are feature-guarded and off by default.

Run/verify: included scripts and docs (docs/runbooks/dr/staged-switchover.md and scripts/dr/run_switchover_test.sh) with step-by-step expected outputs and expected metric changes. A CI job (ci/dr-validation.yml) was added that runs the Terraform module in dry-run mode and executes a non-invasive subset of the playbook to assert readiness and routing. This CI is gated and opt-in for main until teams have signoff.

Rollback and safety: all actions are idempotent and reversible; the playbooks include explicit rollback handlers for each stage (control-plane restore, ipvlan route cleanup, KV cache invalidation). The Terraform module uses a short-lived resource tagging pattern and deletes ephemeral infra in the teardown phase. A forced abort will run the rollback handlers and attempt best-effort cleanup.

Files changed (high level): list below includes the primary artifacts changed. Small templates and script snippets are included; no model code or runtime kernels changed.

Related work: ENG-9272 (DR readiness initiative) and PM-814 (customer validation program). This builds on prior runbook efforts but aims to provide CI-first validation that can be scheduled as an automated rehearsal.

Checklist: [x] ansible playbook implemented, [x] terraform test module, [x] helm chart opt-in hooks, [x] docs/runbook written, [x] CI job added (opt-in), [x] reviewers: engineering and SRE signoff requested.

Notes for reviewers: focus on safety fences and idempotency; validate the Terraform tagging/teardown logic; confirm the Helm hooks are truly opt-in and don't run in production installs by default.

feat(ansible): staged switchover playbook with rollback handlers
chore(helm): add switchover hook template and values toggle
docs: staged switchover runbook and quick reference
review_comments: Ethan Cole: left inline notes on the teardown sequence — prefer explicit resource deletion over rely-on-expiry; see installer/terraform/modules/dr-test/main.tf:24
Priya Nair: addressed by adding explicit destroy calls and tagging resources with 'dr-test' for deterministic selection; added a teardown.sh wrapper
Marta Ruiz: approved after confirming Helm hooks are toggled by values.switchover.enabled=false by default
Samir Patel: requested additional assertions around KV cache invalidation; added a short probe and a metric assertion step in playbook stage 2
notes_for_ops: This PR introduces opt-in test artifacts only. To enable validation in a private cluster, set values.switchover.enabled=true and follow docs/runbooks/dr/staged-switchover.md. The terraform test module requires credentials with minimal provisioning rights; document lists the least-privilege IAM policy sample.
backport_notes: No backports scheduled; changes are additive and opt-in.
